clue.text: Severely punish, making someone accept work forcibly?

definitions.meaning: to punish someone with the full rigour of the law
literally hurling a volume, a written work, at someone so they must take it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to impose the harshest available penalty, as if by every rule in the statute volume.

clue.text: Social conventions awfully stern, restricting competent fellow

indicators.note: the jumbled letters enclose the next pieces
awfully says the letters of stern are badly arranged

parts.note: able means competent
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: Etiquette can be terribly strict, keeping a capable chap in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles stern to TNERS, and 'restricting' puts ABLEMAN after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite behaviour while eating is an example of social conventions.

clue.text: Sound of horse in river

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word pronounced like the one for this horse

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat

explanation.surface: A horse is heard neighing in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river of Switzerland and France.

clue.text: Ethos went sloppy — one should get things sharpened up

definitions.text: one should get things sharpened up

indicators.note: sloppy work is untidy, so these letters are messed up

explanation.surface: The spirit of a place has gone slack, and someone should sharpen things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone used for honing blades, the tool by which knives are made keen.

clue.text: Sheltering in coal scuttle is little primate

indicators.note: the small word shelters inside the container

parts.note: a hod is a coal scuttle
mini means little

explanation.surface: A small primate hides in a coal bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the family of great apes and humans, which are primates.

clue.text: Derek, an artist, establishing wine stores

parts.note: Bo Derek, the actress
Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A man called Derek, who paints, sets up wine shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Derek is a surname here: Bo Derek, star of the film 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish wine shops or cellars storing wine.

clue.text: Order whale-hunter to finish early and beach in time of war

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: the last letter of the name is lost

parts.note: Captain Ahab hunts the white whale in Moby-Dick

explanation.surface: A whaling captain is ordered to stop early and land on a wartime beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha Beach was a D-Day landing site in Normandy in 1944.

clue.text: The final minutes of football? That could briefly make our tour!

definitions.meaning: the extra minutes at the end of a match for stoppages

definitions.text: That could briefly make our tour!
definitions.meaning: with time shortened to its letter T, putting T on 'our' gives 'tour'

explanation.definitionFit: Stoppage minutes tacked on at the end of a football match.

clue.text: Drink coming in dribble at back of pub

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here the end of pub

parts.note: to dribble is to ooze, leak slowly

explanation.surface: Someone sees a drink dribbling at the back of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: alcoholic drink in general is called this.

clue.text: Region of intellectuals including exceptional lad

indicators.note: the word for intellectuals holds the next piece within it

parts.note: great minds are intellectuals

indicators.note: something exceptional is out of the ordinary, so the letters of lad are put out of order

explanation.surface: A part of the country full of clever people also includes one unusual boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts ALD, the anagram of lad, inside MINDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name for the central area of England, a region of the country.

clue.text: Among atheists he is pink

definitions.meaning: in the word atheists the letters he sit just before the middle

explanation.definitionFit: Pink describes someone holding moderately socialist political views.

clue.text: American philosopher, this writer entertained by Elizabeth and Charles?

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host sits inside the host's letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher
the setter referring to himself, ME
Charles is the son of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A US thinker is hosted by a royal couple, Elizabeth and Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; Charles, her eldest child, stands for SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the nineteenth-century American transcendentalist essayist and thinker.

clue.text: Any number put in rank alongside Eastern VIP

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for rank

parts.note: a grade is a rank or level
N is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Some figure is given a ranking next to an important person from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish nobleman of the highest rank, hence any very important person.

clue.text: Past would include gross conduct you'd expect from yobs

indicators.note: the word for past holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR is a standard abbreviation for gross, twelve dozen

explanation.surface: In the past there was disgusting behaviour from thugs.
explanation.walkthrough: A yob is British slang for a loutish young man.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggressive, troublemaking behaviour typical of hooligans.

clue.text: Neglectful learner out getting drunk to sink towards the floor

indicators.note: the drunk letters stagger into a new order
the learner's letter is removed

parts.note: L is a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A careless student gets drunk and slumps to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes one L from Neglectful; 'getting drunk' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bend the knee in worship, lowering oneself to the ground.

clue.text: Action of bailiffs in school? There's anguish, not half, about that

indicators.note: the shortened word for anguish is wrapped about the next piece
only the first half of the word for anguish is kept

parts.note: distress is anguish
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant happens at a school, causing great anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: School is a verb here, to train, not a building; 'not half' keeps the front half of the anguish word and 'about' wraps that round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal seizure of goods to settle a debt, carried out by bailiffs.

clue.text: Others with agitation mounting about Conservative limits

parts.note: the rest are the others

indicators.note: the turned word goes about the next letter
in a down clue, mounting reads the word upwards

parts.note: a stir is agitation

explanation.surface: Others in a fuss about a Tory curbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns STIR into RITS, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to limit, keep within bounds.

clue.text: Someone who is ignored — object?

definitions.meaning: a person treated as if they did not exist
a thing, something that is not a human being at all

explanation.definitionFit: The term means a person whose existence is officially denied, and literally a thing that is no person.

clue.text: Time to get stuck into a bit of dressmaking or cooking?

indicators.note: the letter is pushed inside the word

parts.note: sewing is part of making dresses

explanation.surface: Time is needed for some dressmaking or cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewing is a kind of cooking by slow simmering.

clue.text: Journalist gets first sniff of scandal probing cardinal

indicators.note: the letter goes into the cardinal's name

parts.note: Cardinal John Henry Newman

indicators.note: just the first letter of scandal is taken

explanation.surface: A reporter scents a scandal involving a cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter or journalist working for a newspaper.

clue.text: Bank at sea? Say nothing, little troublemaker!

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
an elf is a small mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: Someone at the seaside tells a naughty child to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental shelf is an underwater bank or ledge of seabed.

clue.text: Big leader off, free to move around as outcast

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the trimmed word
the letters of free move into a new order
the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: huge means big

explanation.surface: A big boss leaves, at liberty to wander as an exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges free into REFE; 'leader off' drops the first letter; 'around' puts the jumbled letters round the rest. Big is a synonym, not a description of the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driven from their homeland is an exile, a kind of outcast.

clue.text: Fertiliser put on with summer month coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
AUG is August

explanation.surface: Fertiliser spread in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seabird droppings used as manure, a fertiliser.

clue.text: Cricketer outside his own country, spinning in theatre of combat

indicators.note: the cricketer's name goes outside the next piece

parts.note: Shane Warne, the famous Australian leg-spin bowler

indicators.note: the letters for the country are turned round

parts.note: OZ is slang for Australia, Warne's homeland

explanation.surface: An Australian spin bowler playing abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' reverses the country, apt since Shane Warne was a celebrated Australian spin bowler; 'outside' puts his name around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the area where fighting takes place.

clue.text: Nothing holy? Hesitation to give biased description of people's religion

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
pi is slang for pious
um expresses hesitation

explanation.surface: Is nothing sacred? Marx gave his skewed view of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Karl Marx called religion 'the opium of the people'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx's famous jibe: religion was the drug of the masses.

clue.text: Games I'll run, sticking to the rules excessively

indicators.note: the letters run into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sports official will run the contests by the book, perhaps too strictly.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive adherence to law or formula; strict literalism about regulations.

clue.text: Section of rock, cold material

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
lint is a soft fabric used for dressings

explanation.surface: Part of a rock face is chilly cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological term for a block of limestone pavement separated by fissures.

clue.text: One chum gets one agitated and all that sort of thing

definitions.text: and all that sort of thing

indicators.note: agitated letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A friend finds someone getting worked up about everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin tag meaning and everything of that kind, used like et cetera.
